notes: No web search. The session's web search allowance was already spent when this part began (its first search was refused), so nothing here comes from the search tool and no search engine was read in its place. Everything was found by reading known addresses with the kit's honest User-Agent, one request at a time, each site's robots.txt read first: each government's own site, the state parties' and their local units' sites, the Legislative Reference Library, the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read on a scratch copy of the database with the files step), a few addresses guessed from a candidate's name (an address lookup first, then one request), and local news organizations' election pages reached from their front pages (on Eden Prairie Local News also through the site's own search box, which its robots.txt allows).

A question for John, and what was set aside because of it. Every page a finding rests on is allowed by its site's robots.txt for the kit's User-Agent, checked the way the kit's own reader does it. But this part was run by one of Anthropic's models, and four sites it read carry a list in robots.txt asking Anthropic's named agents to stay out (ClaudeBot and anthropic-ai on all four, Claude-Web on three), although the kit's own name is not on the list: hometownsource.com (the Sun newspapers, ABC Newspapers, the Monticello Times, the Morrison County Record), presspubs.com (the Shoreview Press), re-electbirdman.org (a campaign site built on CampaignPartner) and sd8dfl.org (the Senate District 8 DFL, with Squarespace's switch against AI crawlers turned on). The lists were noticed only after the pages had been read. Rather than decide for John whether such a list binds the kit, nothing from those four sites is among the findings; what they would have given is under held_for_john at the end of this file, each with its page, so that John can open the page himself or say the kit may use it. They were not opened again after the lists were noticed, and the second reader should not open them for this part. On hometownsource.com the site's own search box was used seven times before that. Where a site names Claude-User, the name for a reader acting on a person's request, nothing past its front page was asked for: the Wahpeton Daily News and the Forum Communications papers (West Central Tribune, Detroit Lakes Tribune). The Proctor Journal and the Waseca County News carry lists like hometownsource.com's. Of these five only the front pages had been asked for, and nothing is kept from them. News sites with no such list were read and are cited: Eden Prairie Local News and the Pine Knot News.

Left alone, and nothing worked around: jordanrasmusson.com, markthell.com, stevenscountytimes.com and Pope County's site (each answered with a bot check; whether markthell.com is the candidate's is not known, so nothing is recorded about it); Becker County's site (its newer address shows a bot-check page, and its older address presents a certificate chain that neither the kit's reader nor the fetch tool, tried once, could verify; certificate checking is never switched off), so David Meyer has no findings; Wilkin County's and the City of Sauk Rapids' sites (their robots.txt asks unlisted scripts to stay out), so Steven Arnhalt and Nicholas Sauer have no findings; the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (it answers 403, robots.txt included), so the two judges have no official page; the Austin Daily Herald (403); the Pope County Tribune's search page (robots.txt).

Michael D. Wentzell: the website he filed with the Secretary of State (judgewentzell.com, with or without www) now leads to a registrar's holding page ("A Brand New Domain!"), so no website is recorded for him. Gregory M. Davids filed none; gregdavids.com exists but is a parked page.

Candidates with nothing found, beyond those named above: Tabitha Johnson (not on the City of Fairmont's council page or any of its nine board pages); Nicholas A Prozinski, Allison Hoffbauer and Elizabeth Griebel (none is on their district's list of sitting board members; Glencoe-Silver Lake's own page of candidates' answers names no public office or website for Liz Griebel); Laurence J. party_support (a key the loader does not read): the Senate District 34 DFL lists Thomas Huling under "Letter of Support Candidates", apart from its endorsed candidates. As in other parts of this sweep it is kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls it an endorsement; whether and how it is shown is John's decision. A lead for the endorsements step, about people who are not in this part: the Senate District 35 Republicans' page (https://www.sd35gop.com/recommended-candidat.html) has a table headed "Nonpartisan local offices up for election in 2026", described as candidates the unit heard from at its June meeting and "a partial list", that names Pat Carlson (Coon Rapids Mayor) and Brian Armstrong (Coon Rapids City Council, Ward 5), the other candidates in two of this part's races. It does not call them endorsed.

Terra Fleming's birth year is worked out from her campaign site's sentence about a 60th birthday "this July", not printed there as a year; the reasoning is beside the finding. A newspaper's questionnaire prints an age for Thuba Nguyen; an age on a given day is not a birth year, so none is recorded for her.

For the second reader: two sources are harder to open than a web page. Carlton County's minutes of January 8, 2019 draw their text inside form objects, which the kit's PDF reader does not read (a browser shows them); the Moorhead and Waseca school districts' pages are drawn by script, and the lines cited are in the page's own data. The legislators' findings were kept to what the task asks for sitting members (website, endorsements, review items), plus public offices outside the Legislature that the Library's records give for two of them.

Privacy. The reader used for this part masks e-mail addresses, telephone numbers and street addresses before a page is shown, and candidates' statements were read for sentences about public offices, websites and party. Before the mask and that narrowing were in place, some pages were shown whole or in part to this session's output: three campaign sites' own pages about the candidate, the Library's record for one legislator, one school district's page of candidates' answers, candidates' profiles in news stories (family, religion, schooling, employers and ages appear on them), and two board members' office telephone numbers and e-mail addresses on Proctor Public Schools' own board page. None of it is recorded here or anywhere else.
